task.description: Re-review REQ-061's diff after rework iteration 1 fixed a real gap: dispatch_task_completion_hop_chain/5 now correctly routes a downstream (not just same-hop) :no_matching_edge error into the shared ExecutionError sink. Your PREVIOUS PASS (step-02d-reviewer.json) signed off on AC4's interim reading as 'REQ-049 and REQ-050, the 2 currently-shippable callers, both wired' -- that was WRONG in a way this rework partially, not fully, corrects. The accurate picture now is: REQ-050's realistic scenario IS now genuinely wired and demonstrated by a real passing test (fixed this rework). REQ-049's call site remains UNREACHABLE due to a separate, pre-existing gap in already-shipped REQ-049 code (merge_output_variables/5 always passes nil for variable_validations) -- filed as docs/issues/ISS-0061.yaml rather than fixed here, per Unblock-Everything's scope boundary against expanding into an already-shipped requirement's code. Decide, with this accurate picture in hand: is '1 of 2 currently-reachable callers demonstrated for real (REQ-050), REQ-049 blocked by a filed separate issue, REQ-056/057/062 still future' an acceptable satisfaction of AC4's intent for REQ-061 to ship now, or does this block REQ-061 pending REQ-049's own gap being fixed first (which would be a much larger scope expansion, effectively reopening REQ-049)?

result.summary: Re-reviewed the rework diff (lib/letflow/engine.ex), ISS-0061, and test/letflow/engine_execution_error_test.exs. (1) Idiom: dispatch_task_completion_hop_chain/5's new case-branches on advance_until_stable/4's {:error, {:activation_failed, {:no_matching_edge, ...}}} and the direct {:error, {:no_matching_edge, ...}} same-hop case are both handled as ordinary Ecto.Multi tail routing into the shared ExecutionError.append_multi/3 sink -- no ad hoc process/state-machine crutch, ExecutionError remains the single composable sink per design doc §3/§5.3. Supervision/process-per-instance isolation is untouched (pure Ecto.Multi/Repo.transaction code, no spawn/singleton introduced). (2) Scope: ISS-0061 is a real, well-scoped filing -- root cause (merge_output_variables/5 always passes nil for variable_validations, inherited from REQ-049's own shipped code), evidence (direct code read + AC4b's own test rationale), and explicit boundary citation (Unblock-Everything's scope rule against expanding into an already-shipped requirement) are all present; not a cover for dropped scope, and a GitHub tracking issue is linked. (3) Tests: ran mix test on both files -- 8/8 pass in engine_execution_error_test.exs, 16/16 across it plus engine_complete_task_test.exs, mix compile --warnings-as-errors clean. AC4a is a genuine end-to-end assertion (graph_task_then_gateway_no_match, real complete_task/3 call, asserts {:error, {:instance_execution_error, :no_matching_gateway_edge, {:node, "gw"}}}, EXECUTION_ERROR event count +1, status :error, task stays :pending) -- not weakened. AC4b honestly documents the REQ-049 call site as unreachable via complete_task/3 today and exercises the identical error_args() shape through set_instance_error/2 instead of pretending complete_task/3 coverage exists. (4) AC4 characterization: agree with ORCH's reasoning -- REQ-061's own depends_on is [REQ-048, REQ-050], not REQ-049, so REQ-050's routing being genuinely real and demonstrated end-to-end is the load-bearing part of AC4 for this requirement's sequencing. REQ-049's gap is a pre-existing defect in already-shipped, already-gated code that REQ-061 did not introduce and is not reasonably scoped to fix without reopening REQ-049. '1 of 2 currently-reachable callers demonstrated for real, 1 blocked by a separately-filed pre-existing issue' is an acceptable interim satisfaction of AC4's intent for REQ-061 to ship now. No type-safety gap beyond what ISS-0061 already covers; no new scope creep introduced by the rework fix.
